Definition: A file, ending in .qs, that saves everything placed in a scene: each item, its position, its properties, the cameras and the lights. A new scene project keeps it in the Scenes folder.
A starting program that can be copied and changed. Quorum Studio's scene projects start with one that loads the scene.
The window a Quorum game opens when it runs. A loaded scene is drawn in it.
The part of a game that makes things fall, collide and push on each other.
The part of a game system that turns a scene into pictures on the screen, by sending drawing instructions to the computer's graphics hardware.
A way for programs to draw 2D and 3D graphics, first released in 1992 and used on desktop computers ever since. Quorum uses it unless you ask for Vulkan.
A version of OpenGL that runs inside a web browser. Quorum uses it when a game runs on a web page.
A newer way to draw graphics, first released in 2016. It is faster and gives programs more control. Quorum needs it for terrain, shadows, spotlights and other newer features.
A prediction you can test: a clear statement of what you think will happen and why.
Trying something out, one change at a time, to see whether a hypothesis is right.
